ev_0006.summary: Figure: horizontal solid diameter MN (M(49.96,301), N(524.84,301)) with center O(287.05,300.86); vertical solid segment OP up to P(287,63.16); circle centered O, radius 237.44 px, visible as the upper semicircle (arc from M through the top to N). B(468.98,149.01) lies on the circle (distance from O ~236.9 px). Solid segment B-O (140 deg) and solid segment B-A with A(287,182.36) on OP (interior point, not on the circle). BA is not horizontal (slope about -0.18; B y=149 vs A y=182). M, O, N are collinear and O is the midpoint of MN (radii 237.1 and 237.8). OP is numerically perpendicular to MN, but detect_right_angle_marker found no square mark at O, so the right angle is a candidate only and no right_angle object is emitted. Endpoint overshoots of 2-6 px were snapped to labelled vertices. Labels P, A, B, O, M, N are bound via bind_point_labels; no conflicting letter evidence.

params.instruction: Draw a semicircle figure in TikZ. Use pixel-to-TikZ scale ~ 1 unit = 1 px /100 (e.g. scale=0.01 or compute coordinates so that O is at origin: M=(-2.37,0), N=(2.37,0), P=(0,2.38), O=(0,0)). Upper semicircle centered O radius 2.374 from M to N through top (draw arc 180:0 going through 90, i.e. \draw (M) arc (180:0:2.374)). Solid diameter MN, solid vertical segment O to P (P at top, y=2.38 approx; line goes to P at (0,2.376)). Point A on OP at pixel y=182.36 -> y=(300.86-182.36)/100=1.185 so A=(0,1.185). Point B on the arc at pixel (468.98,149.01): relative x=(468.98-287.05)/100=1.819, y=(300.86-149.01)/100=1.518; draw segments B-O and B-A (solid). Label: P above, A left of point, B upper right, O below-left, M below, N below. Use a small filled dot for points. Keep the output compilable standalone with \documentclass[tikz,border=5pt]{standalone}.
